essentialQuestion.source: How can AI help a community get its problems fixed, and who does the fixing?
essentialQuestion.back: How can AI help get community problems fixed, and who does the fixing?

learningGoal.source: Explain how Traffy Fondue in Thailand uses AI to sort and send residents' reports, why people and agencies still fix the problems, and what its numbers can and can't show.
learningGoal.back: Explain how Traffy Fondue in Thailand uses AI to sort and route residents' reports, why people and agencies still must solve the problems, and what the platform's numbers can and cannot tell.

read.sections.0.text.source: In every city, residents notice problems first: a road with a hole in it, a blocked drain, a street light that has stopped working. Fixing them is the job of the city's offices. But a report has to reach the right office, and in a big city there are many. In Thailand, researchers at NECTEC, part of the country's national science agency, NSTDA, built a platform to help. It is called Traffy Fondue. In May 2022, Bangkok's city government began to use it for reports from residents. Since then, many other towns, offices and agencies across Thailand have joined.
read.sections.0.text.back: In every city residents are the first to notice problems, whether a road with potholes, a blocked drain or a street light that no longer works. Fixing these problems is the job of the city's offices, but a report has to reach the right office, and a big city has very many offices. In Thailand researchers at NECTEC, part of the country's national science agency called NSTDA, built a platform to help. This platform is called Traffy Fondue. In May 2022 Bangkok began using the platform to receive reports from residents. Since then many other cities, offices and agencies across Thailand have joined too.
read.sections.0.text.note: A real Thai platform, so Thai readers may know the names: NECTEC and NSTDA kept in Latin letters as in the English (Thai readers know them as เนคเทค and สวทช.; the abbreviation สวทช. was avoided because the text is read aloud). "Bangkok's city government" = กรุงเทพมหานคร. Thammasat University = มหาวิทยาลัยธรรมศาสตร์ (the checker warns the Latin name is missing; expected).

read.sections.0.simpler.source: In every city, residents see problems first. A road has a hole. A drain is blocked. A street light stops working. The city's offices must fix them. read.sections.0.simpler.back: In every city residents see problems first. Roads have potholes, drains get blocked, street lights stop working. The city's offices must fix these problems, but a report has to reach the right office. A big city has many offices. In Thailand researchers at the national science agency built a platform to help. This platform is called Traffy Fondue. In May 2022 Bangkok began using it. Later other cities and agencies in Thailand joined.

read.sections.1.heading.source: What the AI does, and what people do
read.sections.1.heading.back: What AI does, and what people do

read.sections.1.text.source: To make a report, a resident uses LINE, a messaging app. They send a photo, a few words and the place. Then AI reads the report and sorts it by type, such as roads, flooding or lights. The system sends it to the office that should deal with it. Sorting and sending is the AI's part of the work. After that, people take over. Officials check the report and decide what to do. Some jobs need only a repair team. A bigger job may need money, a plan and more time. The AI routes the report. People and agencies do the fixing.
read.sections.1.text.back: To report, residents use LINE, a messaging app. They send a photo, a short description and the location. Then AI reads the report and sorts it by type, such as roads, flooding or street lighting. The system sends the report to the office that should look after it. Sorting and sending reports is the part of the work AI does. After that, people take over. Officials check the report and decide what to do. Some jobs need only a repair team; bigger jobs may need more money, plans and time. AI passes reports on, while people and agencies solve the problems.

read.sections.1.simpler.source: A resident makes a report in LINE, a messaging app. They send a photo, some words and where it is. Then AI reads the report. It sorts it by type, like roads or floods. It sends it to the right office. That is the AI's part. Then people take over. Officials check the report and send workers. A big job needs money and a plan too. So the AI routes the report. People and agencies fix the problem.
read.sections.1.simpler.back: Residents report in LINE, a messaging app. They send a photo, a description and say where it is. Then AI reads the report. It sorts it by type, such as roads or flooding. It sends the report to the right office. That is AI's part. Then people take over. Officials check the report and send workers. Big jobs need money and plans too. So AI passes reports on, while people and agencies solve problems.

read.sections.2.heading.source: What the numbers can and can't show
read.sections.2.heading.back: What the numbers can and cannot tell

read.sections.2.text.source: Bangkok says it received 588,842 reports in two years and resolved about 79% of them. These numbers come from the city and the platform's makers, and "resolved" means an official closed the case. In 2025, Bangkok's governor told officials not to close cases with photos that had nothing to do with the problem. So a closed case is not always a fixed problem. In 2025, researchers at Thammasat University in Bangkok studied 98,000 reports and talked with 12 people who knew the system. They found it helped the city see where problems were and plan repairs. They also noted that it needs a smartphone and the internet, which not everyone has.
read.sections.2.text.back: Bangkok says it received 588,842 reports in two years and finished fixing about 79 percent. These numbers come from the city and the platform's makers, and “finished fixing” means officials closed the case. In 2025 Bangkok's governor ordered officials not to close cases with photos unrelated to the problem. So a closed case does not always mean the problem was fixed. In 2025 researchers from Thammasat University in Bangkok studied 98,000 reports and talked with 12 people who know the system well. They found the system helps the city see where problems are and plan repairs. They also said the system needs a smartphone and internet, which not everyone has.
read.sections.2.text.note: Bangkok's governor = ผู้ว่าราชการกรุงเทพมหานคร; "close a case" = ปิดเรื่อง. Check these are the usual terms for Traffy Fondue in Thai news.

read.sections.2.simpler.source: Bangkok says it got 588,842 reports in two years. It says about 79% were resolved. These numbers come from the city and the makers. Resolved means an official closed the case. In 2025, the city's leader warned officials about one problem. Some closed cases with photos that did not show the problem. So a closed case is not always a fixed problem. University researchers studied 98,000 reports. It helped the city plan repairs, they found. But it needs a smartphone and the internet.
read.sections.2.simpler.back: Bangkok says it received 588,842 reports in two years and says it finished fixing about 79 percent. This number comes from the city and the makers. Finished fixing means officials closed the case. In 2025 the city's leader warned officials about a problem: some closed cases with pictures that did not show the problem. So a closed case is not always a fixed problem. University researchers studied 98,000 reports. They found the system helps the city plan repairs, but the system needs a smartphone and internet.

watch.summary.source: In this video, people who build and study AI talk about fairness. AI tools learn from data, and they are already used in many parts of life. The speakers say AI could help more people get what they need. But AI can also be unfair. If the data, or the people who build a tool, leave some groups out, the tool can work worse for those groups or treat them unfairly. This is called algorithmic bias. The speakers say that people from many different backgrounds should help to build AI. They also say that people must keep checking AI tools, so that the tools help everyone and don't harm the people they leave out.
watch.summary.back: In this video people who build and study AI talk about fairness. AI tools learn from data and are already used in many areas of life. The speakers say AI might help more people get what they need, but AI can also be unfair. The speakers say people from many backgrounds should help build AI, and also that people must keep checking AI tools so the tools help everyone and do not harm people who are overlooked.

educatorNotes.0.source: What the sources establish (claims/DW10.md). Traffy Fondue was developed by NECTEC, part of Thailand's National Science and Technology Development Agency (NSTDA). Bangkok's city government launched it on 31 May 2022 (Hansen and Dahiya, 2025); residents report through a LINE chatbot with a photo, a description, a category and the place. The researchers describe an AI engine that sorts reports into categories and a workflow that sends each to the responsible agency; NSTDA's 2024 statement adds AI summaries, suggested priorities and filtering of rude language. Repairs are done by the agencies, their teams or contractors; bigger jobs go through evaluation, budgeting and a project. All the scale and speed figures are the city's or the makers' own: Bangkok's 588,842 reports in two years with about 79% resolved (June 2024, from the governor's report, "resolved" not defined); NSTDA's 2026 page (all 77 provinces, 34,786 agencies, over 2 million resolved tickets, average resolution time down from 90 to 15 days). No independent check of repair quality was found. The Thammasat study (98,000 reports, May to December 2022, 12 interviews) reports 84% satisfaction and estimated savings, and notes the platform is digital-first.
educatorNotes.0.back: What sources confirm (claims/DW10.md): Traffy Fondue was developed by NECTEC, part of the National Science and Technology Development Agency (NSTDA). Bangkok began using it on 31 May 2022 (Hansen and Dahiya, 2025). Residents report through a LINE chatbot with a photo, description, category and location. Researchers describe an AI system that sorts reports into categories and a workflow that sends each case to the responsible agency. NSTDA's 2024 statement adds AI summarising, priority suggestions and profanity filtering. Repairs are done by agencies, their teams or contractors; bigger jobs go through assessment, budgeting and becoming projects. All figures for scale and speed are the city's or makers' own: Bangkok's 588,842 reports in two years with about 79 percent resolved (June 2024, from the governor's report; “resolved” not defined) and NSTDA's 2026 web page (all 77 provinces, 34,786 agencies, more than 2 million cases resolved, average resolution time down from 90 days to 15). No independent check of repair quality was found. The Thammasat study (98,000 reports, May to December 2022, 12 interviews) reports 84 percent satisfaction and estimated cost savings, and notes the platform is mainly digital-first.

Lessons 16 and 17 mention Traffy Fondue again briefly.
